thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager P1 — embeddings pipeline: sudden KV-evict spike in us-west-2 affecting embedder service. link: https://monitoring/replays/2174993210

ana: I'm on it. seeing evict-worker respawn loop on nodes 3-6. restarting worker on host-ukg-03, tailing logs now.

maria: noted customer impact: some ingest and embedding requests failing. Do we have quick numbers?

ana: quick stats from logs: ~3.2% 5xx for embeddings over last 10m, p95 latency for /v1/embeddings up from ~120ms -> ~620ms. Customers A and C have elevated error rates.

jamal: tagging infra - @kevin can you look at disk IO and scheduler backlog for those hosts?

kevin: on it. I see GC + eviction thrash causing worker stalls. killed a stuck thread on host-ukg-04 which immediately dropped local qps. investigating scheduler queue.

ana: mitigation applied: scaled embedder pool + pinned fallback model variant for affected customers (rollout id: rollback-embed-2026-03-15). Commands I ran:
```
# scale up embed pool
rctl scale --pool embed-usw-2 --replicas 6
# pin lighter variant for critical custs
rctl route --customer A --model embed-lite:v1.3
```

maria: good. can we add a temporary routing rule for critical customers only until postmortem?

kevin: yes, created rule-2026-03-15-critical-route. fallback to embed-lite for customers with SLA flag.

sre-bot: Auto-note: Severity=P1. Triage leads notified. Incident channel created.

ana: monitoring: errors dropping to 0.7% and p95 down to ~220ms after scale+pin. I'll keep watch for 10m then handoff to next oncall.

jamal: nice. capture mitigation steps and open a postmortem ticket so we can track remediation tasks.

ana: creating ticket INF-3987 with summary "KV-evict surge caused embedder latency and errors". adding initial owners and labels.

ana: proposed postmortem meeting — options: tomorrow 09:30 PT or Friday 10:00 PT. who can attend?

maria: I can run the doc and own remediation tracking. Friday 10:00 PT works best for me.

kevin: Friday 10:00 PT works for infra.

jamal: I'll join Friday to help size infra work.

ana: cc @maria I'll paste a concise timeline and mitigation steps into the ticket.

ana: timeline snippet:
- 10:04 incident-bot paged
- 10:06 ana confirmed evict-worker respawn loop
- 10:12 scaled pool + pinned fallback variant for SLA customers
- 10:16 p95 reduced to ~220ms
- 10:30 monitoring shows stable

maria: initial remediation action items (adding to INF-3987):
1) Root cause deep-dive: kv-evict scheduler interaction with model cache (owner: kevin) — SIZING: large (5-8d)
2) Configurable fallback routing for critical customers (owner: ana) — SIZING: small (1-2d)
3) Canary for embedder memory/evict behavior on new model loads (owner: jamal) — SIZING: medium (3d)
4) Alerting: separate eviction-rate metric + p95 embed latency alarms (owner: maria) — SIZING: small (2d)
5) Post-deploy regression for embedder quantized models (owner: eng-ml) — SIZING: medium (3-4d)

kevin: agree with sizes but split #1 into RCA (3d) + mitigation (2-5d). mark overall as LARGE.

ana: prioritization guidance: this is P1 (customer errors + latency) so recommend mapping to Q2 Reliability OKR: "Reduce embedder incident recurrence by 50%".

jamal: suggested execution order: #1 -> #3 -> #5 -> #4 -> #2. Rationale: fix root cause, introduce canaries/tests, tune alerts, then extend fallback policies.

maria: I'll schedule the Friday postmortem at 10:00 PT and start the doc template. saved link: https://redwood/share/INF-3987-pm-doc

ana: owners recap: kevin (#1), jamal (#3), ana (#2), maria (#4 and PM), eng-ml (#5). please ack with :thumbsup: and add any constraints in the doc.

kevin: :thumbsup: adding initial notes to INF-3987.

jamal: :thumbsup: drafting canary plan and will post PR for review.

maria: if anyone wants these items in the Q2 sprint board, add a one-line justification + expected metric improvement to the PM doc so we can size during planning.

ana: final: no active customer outages now. monitoring watch for next 24h. we'll reconvene at the postmortem to firm up action items and scope. thanks all. :white_check_mark:
